catalog_quote: In all languages under study except those of Lau (LAU and VBL), the penultimate stress rule is qualified by the rule that stress always falls on the first vowel of a low or mid to high vowel sequence. In Lau, however, there is no qualification to the penultimate stress rule, so it is the second vowel of such a sequence that is stressed when it occurs in penultimate position. Thus we may contrast: NWN 'ráica' 'see it' / LAU 'raíca'; ONO 'ráuta' 'enough' / VBL 'raúta'. [p. 68] ... It has been observed in section 3.10 that, in all Fijian languages except those of Lau, it is the first vowel in a low or mid to high sequence that is always stressed. It is hardly surprising, then, to find instances of loss of the unstressed member of such a sequence, especially since such sequences occurring in penultimate position appear to violate the general principle of measure-penultimate stress (Schütz 1976). For example, a word such as raica 'see it' simply conforms to measure-penultimate stress in Lau, as raíca. In most of the rest of Eastern Fiji, it conforms to the competing rule that assigns stress to the first vowel in a rising vowel sequence, as ráica. But in Vanua Levu (LBS, SQN, KRL), the competition between the two rules is removed by the loss of the unstressed vowel, as ráca. [pp. 160-161]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel/syllable (measure-penultimate stress in Schütz's sense), except that in a sequence of a low or mid vowel followed by a high vowel (ai, au, ei, eu, oi, ou) the stress falls on the first vowel of the sequence even when the high vowel is penultimate; thus ráica 'see it', ráuta 'enough'. Gone Dau is one of the 38 communalects surveyed and is not in Lau, so it falls under this rule; Table 12 shows Gone Dau has gone furthest (100%) in dropping the resulting unstressed penultimate high vowel (rau 'leaf' > ra).
new_statements.exceptions: Lau varieties (LAU, VBL) have no diphthong qualification (raíca). Sec. 3.9 phrase-antepenultimate a-lengthening applies only to the Western communalects (not Gone Dau).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (measure-penultimate) stress stated as a rule shared by all communalects surveyed; the diphthong qualification is the only variable. The statement covers Gone Dau by inclusion in the 38-communalect survey, not by a Gone Dau-specific sentence.
new_statements.identity_note: Geraghty 1979 treats Gone Dau as communalect 27 (GOD), villages Tavea and Galoa (Bua); the Gone Dau islands also include Yaqaga (now speaking Navakasiga) and Macuata-i-wai (slightly different; the variety Capell & Lester 1942 knew). Classified Eastern Fijian but a relic area sharing Western traits. Glottolog gone1237 = Gone Dau/Gonedau (goo), same entity. The stress statement is a survey-wide generalisation over all 38 communalects (except Lau), not a Gone Dau-specific sentence.
